_REGENERATION_IS_GATED_BYTE_IDENTICAL: tests/test_arc_executor_migrated.py::test_ex6_the_seed_REGENERATES_byte_identically re-runs this builder and diffs.  The Term idioms are IMPORTED from tools/build_arc_goals_seed.py, so if MEASURE_EPOCH or the pool predicate ever changes there, this seed goes out of date LOUDLY instead of silently diverging.
_SELF_LOAD_ONLY_RATIONALE: substrate/boot_all.py::_read_seeds GLOBS seeds/*.json and installs every match at boot, so a file here is live in EVERY agent in the tree the moment it lands.  seeds/arc_goals.json and seeds/arc_magnitude.json both ship self_load_only for that reason and this seed keeps the gating: an executor that dispatches jobs is the LAST thing that should arrive in every agent by a glob.  Activation is one key and a paired tree-wide sweep.
_SOFT_DEPENDENCY_ON_arc_magnitude: v1.1.0 (A11/WH1) wires ax_dispatch to the ORDER-N collapse (mg_sel_agid, seeds/arc_magnitude.json) when that collapse is live on the graph, and to the order-1 collapse (arc_sel_agid) when it is not.  arc_magnitude is DELIBERATELY NOT in depends_on: it is self_load_only, every EX1-EX6 scene boots without it, and making it hard would both change what those scenes boot and put an order-N collapse into every graph that merely wants hands.  The branch is a Term in the rule (SEL_AGID), never a Python conditional, and the order records which branch it took.
description: AG-5 -- THE EXECUTOR AND THE STATUS LIFECYCLE.  Two independent rungs converged on this as the blocker: the arc-goal rung called itself 'a planning layer with no hands', and the magnitude rung found decomposition blocked because a parent goal must LEAVE THE POOL and nothing in this tree ever wrote a terminal status.  This seed is the missing seam, and it is four rules. ax_dispatch turns the arc-grain collapse's winner into an ExecOrder, routed by route_pick's own Argmin-over-cues shape, and is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of ordering a goal whose kind has no ExecClass.  v1.1.0 (A11/WH1): the collapse it binds is the ORDER-N one (mg_sel_agid) whenever that collapse is live, falling back to order-1 (arc_sel_agid) when it is not -- because AG-5 SS8.9 measured that the two DISAGREE and that order-N picks the one goal the executor can run, with no human reply in the scene.  ax_retired_epoch stamps when a goal went terminal.  ax_rearm is the anti-oscillation latch: a retired goal re-enters the pool only when its source residual is genuinely stale again AND the measurement epoch has advanced.  ax_close makes a completed execution countable. THE EPOCH ITSELF: `arc_measure_epoch` was a counter with no producer, and every expiry mechanism in the two rungs below turns on it.  The adapter bumps it WHEN AND ONLY WHEN a measurement actually ran, so an unconditioned answer's one-epoch life is now measured in measurements. v1.2.0 (A13/WH4(c)) adds a fifth rule, ax_impotent: `ag_ask` fires on a TIE, and A11/A12 found the case it cannot see -- a non-empty pool in which NOTHING is routable, no tie anywhere, the loop stopping and saying nothing (WH2 SS3.1 iteration 1).  ax_impotent mints AgendaVerdict{kind:'impotent'} QUANTIFIED OVER THE WHOLE POOL (Not(Exists(POOL(), g, dispatchable(g))) -- dispatchable is ax_dispatch's OWN routability test, reused verbatim), never the winner alone, so a pool holding one routable goal ranked below the winner is correctly NOT impotent.  Mint-once is keyed on the pool's own SIGNATURE (its ordered agid list, JSON-encoded) rather than the tick, and the verdict lapses through the EXISTING, UNMODIFIED gr_condition_lapse via a fact_equals(arc_measure_epoch) condition -- zero new mechanism, zero new DSL Term. v1.3.0 (A15) adds a SECOND ExecClass row (local_id 4011): the structural-ceiling residual (arc6.structural.enum_op_table), re-measured by scripts/arc6_remeasure_structural.py.  ZERO new rules -- ax_dispatch/ROUTE/_routable/_dispatchable already filter over EVERY ExecClass node via the three-part key (kind + evidence_artifact + source_rid), so a second class is SEED DATA, not a rule edit.  This is the ceiling probe on the executor's own reach: A10-A14 each independently measured that reach as exactly ONE ExecClass; this is the second. v1.4.0 (A18) adds a SIXTH rule, ax_world_probe_epoch: EXECUTOR.md SS5 named, reported not patched, the re-arm DEADLOCK -- the epoch has exactly one producer (run_order, after RUNNING a measurement) and a retired goal cannot be run, so a genuinely re-failed condition on a retired goal could never bring it back on its own, and A15's own extension probe showed the natural end state of BOTH shipped ExecClasses retiring leaves ZERO executable pool members, not one -- the ordinary case, not a corner case.  ax_world_probe_epoch does not touch ax_rearm or its conjunction; it adds a SECOND, INDEPENDENT epoch producer that never runs anything: a retired goal whose condition is confirmed genuinely re-failed on TWO SEPARATE, externally-triggered probes (the adapter's refresh_evidence_facts, already existing, now carrying its own PRIOR reading across the probe-call boundary as stale_at_last_probe) while the epoch has sat still since its retirement gets `world_drift_confirmed` stamped; the adapter reads that as a pure query and bumps arc_measure_epoch the same mechanical way run_order does.  A SINGLE probe cannot satisfy the guard -- the discriminator against reintroducing the churn EX4 measured ax_rearm's own two-sided latch against. v1.5.0 (A19) adds a SEVENTH and EIGHTH rule, ax_fallback_silent and ax_fallback_cleared: WIRE_HANDS SS8.1 named, first on its own damage-ordered list, THE SILENT ORDER-N FALLBACK -- SEL_AGID reverting to order-1 when mg_sel_agid is absent is a deliberate, measured design (SS1.2, untouched by this rung), but nothing on the graph said so beyond a per-order breadcrumb (selected_by). THE FALLBACK ITSELF DOES NOT CHANGE.  ax_fallback_silent mints AgendaVerdict{kind:'order_n_fallback', active:1.0} the instant _order_n_is_not_live() holds -- the SAME Term SEL_AGID itself branches on, imported verbatim, never re-derived -- and no currently-active verdict of this kind already exists (ax_impotent's own mint-once shape).  ax_fallback_cleared flips `active` to 0.0 the instant order-N IS live: a DIRECT REVERSIBLE PAIR, the gr_condition_lapse/gr_condition_hold SHAPE, but keyed on the live Term rather than an epoch, because arc_magnitude can be loaded onto an ALREADY-RUNNING graph with no epoch bump anywhere in the scene (test_wh3_* vs test_wh1_* differ by exactly this).  Zero new DSL Term, zero new node type, zero new edge type (AgendaVerdict/has_agenda_verdict are already-declared productions), zero new adapter function -- agenda_verdicts(sub, 'order_n_fallback') is already generic. ax_dispatch/SEL_AGID/ARMED_AGID/ARMED_VALUE/COLLAPSE_NAME/_armed/ROUTE/_routable are BYTE-UNCHANGED: this rung only adds observability, it does not change when the fallback fires. v1.6.0 (A20) adds a NINTH and TENTH rule, ax_ask_divergence_active and ax_ask_divergence_cleared: the SAME direct-reversible-pair shape as A19, applied to a DIFFERENT question -- given that the order-N collapse IS live, does it name the SAME goal ag_ask asked about.  Mints/clears AgendaVerdict{kind:'ask_dispatch_divergence'} by comparing SEL_AGID() against arc_sel_agid, both stamps already read/written elsewhere.  ag_ask/seeds/arc_goals.json are BYTE-UNCHANGED. v1.7.0 (A21) adds an ELEVENTH and TWELFTH rule, ax_impotent_pool_lapse and ax_impotent_pool_hold: PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC6_IMPOTENCE_TERM.md SS8 item 1 / PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC6_IMPOTENCE_CAMPAIGN.md SS9 item 6 named the LAST originally-named remaining gap in this executor sub-thread -- an impotent verdict's condition lapses (gr_condition_lapse, unmodified) only on an EPOCH bump, never on the POOL'S OWN MEMBERSHIP moving under it within one epoch, so a reader had to compare pool_agids against the current pool by hand.  These two rules add a SECOND, ORTHOGONAL staleness axis (pool_stale) to each impotent verdict, keyed on the SAME _pool_sig() Term ax_impotent itself mints against, live, no epoch involved -- the A19/A20 direct-reversible-pair pattern, applied PER-NODE (not as a global singleton, which would have collapsed IM5's own multi-verdict history) rather than the epoch-shaped fact_equals idiom.  ax_impotent's OWN where/match/mint-once guard is BYTE-UNCHANGED (only its effects gain an additive pool_stale:0.0 stamp at mint), and gr_condition_lapse's closed MISMATCH vocabulary (seeds/goal_residuals.json) is BYTE-UNCHANGED and untouched by this rung. v1.8.0 (A23) adds a THIRTEENTH and FOURTEENTH rule, ax_ask_impotent and ax_ask_impotent_reply: candidate (a) (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC6_IMPOTENCE_CAMPAIGN.md), built NATIVE, not as a naive reuse of ag_ask's own REGION-fallback re-entry gate (A22 SS6 named this the risk; A23's own design investigation confirms question_driver.py's gap-guard/contrast rules do not transfer to this data shape and costs more than the native alternative).  ax_ask_impotent asks a class-scoped question the instant a non-stale AgendaVerdict{kind:'impotent'} exists with no ArcQuestion asked about it yet -- mint-once by the VERDICT's own node identity (an InNeighbours edge-existence guard), the SAME shape ax_impotent itself already uses (pool-signature mint-once) and gap_awareness.json's content-dedup guard uses one seed over -- so a testimony chain that drifts nearest_unroutable_agid across several kinds within one epoch (A22 SS3, already measured) is still asked about EXACTLY ONCE, because it is still the SAME pool state throughout (A14's own headline finding).  ax_impotent/ag_ask/ROUTE/_routable/_dispatchable are BYTE-UNCHANGED: this rule only reads an existing AgendaVerdict, it does not change when one mints. Mints no GoalResidual/testimony (candidate (b) territory, already NO-GO'd by A22) -- ax_ask_impotent_reply only marks the question answered.

attrs.name: default_exec_policy
attrs._confinement_is_STRUCTURAL_not_promised: The executor can act on exactly the goal kinds for which an ExecClass cue exists.  There are TWO (A15), and the dispatch route is an Argmin over the cues matching the goal's THREE-PART key (kind + evidence_artifact + source_rid) -- so a supply_blocker / source_claim / self_concern winner, or a re_measure goal naming neither wired artifact, routes to NOTHING and mints no order.  Adding a class is a seed edit, visible in a diff; it is not something a rule can do.

attrs.name: re_measure
attrs._the_route_key_is_THREE_PART: kind + evidence_artifact + source_rid.  MEASURED: `kind` alone is not enough -- an expired unconditioned testimony mints arc.remeasure.arc.testimony.<region> with kind:'re_measure' and NO evidence_artifact, and a kind-only route would have handed that to this runner.
attrs.description: THE FIRST EXECUTABLE CLASS -- re-measures the row-verdict residual.  A re-measurement goal names an artifact, a condition and a denominator, and the measurement it asks for ALREADY EXISTS AS A SCRIPT -- so executing it is re-running that script on the current binary, which is mechanical I/O.
attrs._runner_is_a_NAME_not_a_command: The adapter resolves this name against a frozen capability table.  A name with no table entry is REFUSED and recorded; the string is never a path, never an argv and never a shell word.

attrs.name: re_measure
attrs._the_route_key_is_THREE_PART: IDENTICAL shape to the first ExecClass -- same three-part key, disambiguated from it by evidence_artifact and source_rid, which is exactly what lets TWO ExecClass rows coexist with ZERO change to _cue_matches/ROUTE/_routable.
attrs.description: THE SECOND EXECUTABLE CLASS (A15) -- re-measures the structural-ceiling residual (`arc6.structural.enum_op_table`).  Picked over the other three unwired residuals (seam A/B/C/D) because its runner (`scripts/arc6_structural_ceiling.py`) has NO third-party dependency and its evidence artifact is not shared with a sibling residual -- see PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC6_SECOND_EXECCLASS.md.  Confirmed live: re-running it on this rung's engine produced GENUINELY DIFFERENT content from the committed evidence (witness_ids grew 7 -> 9), the same 'this is not a tautology, it can move' standard AG-5 SS2.2 applies to the row-verdict residual's own condition.
attrs._runner_is_a_NAME_not_a_command: Same capability-table permission boundary as the first class -- a name with no table entry is REFUSED and recorded; the string is never a path, never an argv and never a shell word.

rules.name: ax_dispatch
rules.comment: AG-5, THE COLLAPSE->ACTION SEAM, AND IT IS route_pick's OWN SHAPE. The DECISION of what to run is this rule; running it is the adapter's mechanical I/O.  Three things are load-bearing and each has a measured reason. (1) THE WINNER IS BOUND BY THE COLLAPSE'S OWN STAMP, never re-ranked -- the ag_select_audit / ag_ask precedent -- AND THE STAMP MUST HAVE SETTLED.  MEASURED: reading the stamp inside the same fixpoint that writes it reads a TRANSIENT, and the first draft of this rule ordered the RUNNER-UP on the shipped boot while the fixpoint's final winner was a different goal.  `_armed` is the two-tick agreement test that closes it, on the winner AND its value. (1b) A11/WH1 -- WHICH COLLAPSE.  This graph carries TWO selections: ag_select's order-1 arc_sel_agid and mg_select's order-N + constraints mg_sel_agid, and AG-5 SS8.9 measured that with the tier ladder installed THEY DISAGREE -- order-1 picks the 42-task blocker (paper inventory at zero discount, no ExecClass, unrunnable) and order-N picks the RE-MEASUREMENT goal, the one this executor can run, WITH NO HUMAN IN THE SCENE.  The hands now follow order-N when it is live and order-1 when it is not (see SEL_AGID) -- a SOFT dependency, because arc_magnitude is self_load_only and every EX1-EX6 scene boots without it.  The fallback is silent, so the order STAMPS which collapse it followed and both stamps as it saw them. (2) CONFINEMENT IS THE EMPTY ARGMIN.  The route is Argmin(Filter(ExecClass, <the THREE-PART key of _cue_matches plus _routable's source_rid check>), priority) and ONE ExecClass ships, so a goal that does not match on ALL THREE routes to null and the Exists guard refuses the mint.  kind ALONE IS NOT THE KEY, and that was measured, not foreseen -- see _cue_matches.  On the SHIPPED graph the winner IS unroutable (the 42-task blocker goal), so this branch is exercised by the boot itself, not by a fixture. (3) THE POOL PREDICATE IS RE-ASSERTED ON THE BOUND GOAL.  ag_select writes arc_sel_agid only while the pool is non-empty, so the stamp can outlive its goal's membership; without this the executor could run a goal that had already retired. SERIALISED TWO WAYS: at most one outstanding order globally, and at most one order per (goal, measurement epoch) -- so re-running the fixpoint cannot mint a second order for the same job, and a job may only recur once a NEW MEASUREMENT has happened.

effects._the_decision_lives_here: which job to run is this rule's Argmin over the route table applied to the collapse's own winner.  The adapter reads `runner` and looks it up in a frozen table; it chooses nothing.

rules.name: ax_retired_epoch
rules.comment: WHEN a goal reached its terminal status.  ag_remeasure_retire (seeds/arc_goals.json, byte-frozen and gated) writes THAT it retired; the anti-oscillation latch below is defined in MEASUREMENT EPOCHS, and until this rung the epoch had no producer, so there was nothing to stamp.  Fires on an ABSENT stamp (`Eq(attr, Lit null)` is this tree's 'absent' test) OR on one ax_rearm has CONSUMED -- the second disjunct is what makes a SECOND retirement get its own epoch instead of inheriting the first one's.  Disjoint from ax_rearm's guard by construction, so the two never contend for the same goal in one pass.

rules.name: ax_rearm
rules.comment: THE ANTI-OSCILLATION LATCH, AND IT IS TWO-SIDED BY CONSTRUCTION. The arc-goal design's SS8.2 guard -- 'a selected goal moves to a terminal status and only re-enters the pool on a measure_epoch bump' -- recorded by that rung as NOT implemented because a terminal status with no executor empties the pool with nothing done.  Now there is an executor. A retired re-measurement goal comes back ONLY when BOTH hold: its source residual is GENUINELY STALE AGAIN (gr_condition_lapse's own verdict, read off the residual -- this rule never re-evaluates a condition), AND the MEASUREMENT EPOCH HAS ADVANCED past the epoch it retired in.  The second half is what makes it a latch rather than a flap: the moment after a re-measurement the residual is un-stale AND the epoch is the retirement epoch, so BOTH halves refuse.  A condition that re-fails inside the same epoch waits; a new measurement without a re-failed condition changes nothing. WHY NOT ag_mint_remeasure.  That rule's mint-once guard is the monotone `remeasure_goal` EDGE LATCH and this engine has no remove_edge, so it can never fire twice for one residual.  Re-arming the EXISTING goal is therefore the only re-entry there is, and it is the better one: the pool never grows a duplicate, and `rearm_count` makes oscillation COUNTABLE.

rules.name: ax_close
rules.comment: AN EXECUTION THAT COMPLETED IS A COUNTABLE GRAPH FACT.  The order closes when its own goal has reached the terminal status -- i.e. when ag_remeasure_retire fired, which happens only if the re-measurement actually un-staled the source residual.  So a CLOSED order is evidence the loop closed, and an order left at `ran` is evidence it did not: the two are distinguishable without reading any adapter return value.

rules.name: ax_impotent
rules.comment: A13/WH4(c) -- TERMINATE HONESTLY, AND IT QUANTIFIES OVER THE WHOLE POOL, NOT THE WINNER.  ag_ask fires on a TIE (margin < threshold under mutual ignorance); this fires on the case it cannot see -- a non-empty pool in which NOTHING is routable, no tie anywhere.  THE GUARD: Not(Exists(POOL(), g, dispatchable(g))) AND the pool is non-empty -- dispatchable is ax_dispatch's OWN routability test (_routable AND Count(mint_source)==1), reused verbatim, so this rule can never disagree with ax_dispatch about what it can run.  A pool with ONE routable member ranked below the winner does NOT fire this -- that is the discriminator against the wrong, winner-only reading (A13 IM2; the SHIPPED BOOT is that scene, unmodified). MINT-ONCE BY POOL SIGNATURE, NOT BY TICK: the guard excludes minting only while a NON-STALE verdict with the SAME pool signature (the ordered agid list, JSON-encoded) already exists, so an unchanged impotent pool never double-mints across repeated run_rules passes, and a GENUINELY different impotent pool (even inside one epoch) mints its own verdict. LAPSES THROUGH THE EXISTING gr_condition_lapse, UNMODIFIED: the verdict carries a holds_under edge to a ResidualCondition with ckind='fact_equals' against arc_measure_epoch, EXACTLY the 'expire at the next measurement' idiom TestimonyPolicy's unconditioned replies already use -- gr_condition_lapse's match (seeds/goal_residuals.json) carries NO type constraint on the node it lapses, so this rides it for free, zero new mechanism. nearest_unroutable_* is DESCRIPTIVE ONLY (SEL_AGID -- whichever collapse is live) and is never read by the firing guard. A21 -- ADDITIVE ONLY: the verdict is now also stamped pool_stale:0.0 at mint (true by construction -- its own pool_agids trivially equals the CURRENT pool signature the instant it mints), read and flipped by ax_impotent_pool_lapse/ax_impotent_pool_hold below.  This where/match/mint-once guard is BYTE-UNCHANGED by A21.

effects._the_decision_lives_here: the firing guard is Not(Exists(POOL(), g, dispatchable(g))) -- the adapter never computes this, never decides it and never even reads it except to render it back for a human.

effects.why: this verdict describes the pool AS OF this measurement epoch; a new measurement may move the world, so it must be re-read rather than re-used once one runs -- the SAME expiry idiom TestimonyPolicy's unconditioned replies already carry (default_condition_fact = arc_measure_epoch).

rules.name: ax_world_probe_epoch
rules.comment: A18 -- THE RE-ARM DEADLOCK, CLOSED WITHOUT RUNNING ANYTHING. PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC6_EXECUTOR.md SS5: 'the executor is the epoch's producer, but it only produces one by RUNNING a goal, and a retired goal is not in the pool to be run.  With exactly one executable goal, a genuinely re-failed condition cannot bring it back on its own.'  MEASURED (PREREG A18 item 3, reusing PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC6_SECOND_EXECCLASS.md SS6's own live probe): the NATURAL trajectory with BOTH shipped ExecClasses retires both re_measure goals and leaves ZERO executable pool members, not one -- the deadlock's precondition is the ORDINARY end state of this loop, not a corner case. THIS RULE IS NOT A SECOND ax_rearm.  It does not touch that rule, does not read arc_measure_epoch to decide anything about a goal's re-entry, and does not widen ax_rearm's own conjunction.  It decides exactly one, narrower thing: whether a RETIRED goal's source residual has genuinely re-failed on TWO SEPARATE, EXTERNALLY-TRIGGERED world probes (r.stale == 1.0 confirmed against r.stale_at_last_probe -- the adapter's own carry of the PREVIOUS refresh_evidence_facts call's reading, the ARM_CARRY precedent applied at the probe-call boundary instead of the fixpoint-tick boundary) while the clock has been stuck since retirement (retired_epoch == the CURRENT epoch, i.e. nothing else has advanced it yet).  A SINGLE probe cannot satisfy this -- stale_at_last_probe still holds the PRIOR, pre-drift reading on the first sighting -- which is the discriminator against collapsing EX4's cell C into cell D (this rung's own AR18b).  Investigated and REJECTED before this rule was written: coupling the epoch bump directly to the SAME single detection event `stale` is already computed from would do exactly that. The adapter reads the resulting fact (world_drift_confirmed) as a PURE QUERY -- the same shape as pending_orders -- and calls the SAME agi.bump_measure_epoch that run_order already calls, mechanically, OUTSIDE run_rules(), so ax_rearm's own epoch-advance check is satisfied only on the NEXT fixpoint, exactly as EX4's cell D already requires manually.  This rule only widens WHICH real-world events can produce the epoch bump ax_rearm has always read; it never runs a measurement and never touches the latch.

rules.name: ax_fallback_silent
rules.comment: A19 -- THE FALLBACK, MADE OBSERVABLE (the ON direction).  WIRE_HANDS SS8.1: 'the fallback is silent... nothing raises an alarm.'  Fires the instant the order-N collapse is not producing a stamp (_order_n_is_not_live(), the SAME Term SEL_AGID itself branches on -- this rule can never disagree with ax_dispatch about which collapse is live, by construction) AND no currently-active verdict of this kind already exists (mint-once, ax_impotent's own shape).  Mints AgendaVerdict{kind:'order_n_fallback', active:1.0} off the SAME agenda hub ax_impotent uses -- a standing, queryable graph fact a self-monitoring agent (or a human, or a future rung) can check PROACTIVELY, rather than inferring the fallback's state order by order from `selected_by`.  Mutually exclusive with ax_fallback_cleared by construction: one reads the Term true, the other reads it false.

effects._the_decision_lives_here: the firing guard is _order_n_is_not_live(), the SAME Term SEL_AGID reads to pick which collapse the hands follow -- the adapter never computes this and never decides it.

rules.name: ax_fallback_cleared
rules.comment: A19 -- THE FALLBACK, MADE OBSERVABLE (the OFF direction, and it is not decoration: a one-way mint would itself be a claim that cannot be revised -- the gr_condition_lapse/gr_condition_hold precedent, quoted almost verbatim).  Fires the instant order-N IS live (Not(_order_n_is_not_live())) while a previously-minted verdict is still marked active, and flips `active` to 0.0.  DELIBERATELY NOT the epoch-shaped fact_equals(arc_measure_epoch) idiom ax_impotent uses: arc_magnitude can be loaded onto an ALREADY-RUNNING graph with no epoch bump anywhere in the scene (exactly how test_wh3_* vs test_wh1_* differ -- one boots without it, one with), so a self-monitoring agent's 'is the fallback active RIGHT NOW' question needs the CURRENT truth of the Term, not a description that stays valid only until the next measurement.  Mutually exclusive with ax_fallback_silent by construction, so the two never contend for the same node in one pass.

rules.name: ax_ask_divergence_active
rules.comment: A20 -- `ag_ask` VS `ax_dispatch`, MADE OBSERVABLE (the ON direction).  WIRE_HANDS SS8 item 4: 'the agent can ask about one goal while acting on another in the same fixpoint... nothing asserts it either way.'  Fires the instant ax_dispatch's OWN target (SEL_AGID()) disagrees with ag_ask's WINNER candidate (arc_sel_agid) AND no currently-active verdict of this kind already exists (mint-once, ax_impotent's /ax_fallback_silent's own shape).  Mints AgendaVerdict{kind:'ask_dispatch_divergence', active:1.0} off the SAME agenda hub ax_impotent/ax_fallback_silent use -- a standing, queryable graph fact a self-monitoring agent (or a human, or a future rung) can check PROACTIVELY, instead of comparing an ArcQuestion's agid_a against an ExecOrder's agid order by order after the fact.  Also stamps whether the dispatch target at least matches ag_ask's OTHER candidate (arc_sel_runner_up_agid) -- descriptive only, never read by any guard -- because A20's own design investigation proved this is true on every scene this seed's shipped policy can reach (the structural bound), and a future policy edit breaking it is precisely the thing this fact exists to catch.

effects._the_decision_lives_here: the firing guard compares SEL_AGID() -- the IDENTICAL Term ax_dispatch's where branches on -- against arc_sel_agid; the adapter never computes this and never decides it, and ag_ask is not read, only its OWN stamp is.

rules.name: ax_ask_divergence_cleared
rules.comment: A20 -- THE OFF DIRECTION, and not decoration: a one-way mint would itself be a claim that cannot be revised -- the gr_condition_lapse/gr_condition_hold precedent, A19's own citation of it, applied a third time.  Fires the instant the two stamps AGREE (or either goes null) while a previously-minted verdict is still marked active, and flips `active` to 0.0.  DELIBERATELY NOT epoch-shaped, same reason as A19's ax_fallback_cleared: a scope or testimony reply can move arc_sel_agid or SEL_AGID() with no epoch bump anywhere in the scene, so a self-monitoring agent's 'do they agree RIGHT NOW' question needs the CURRENT truth of the comparison, not a description valid only until the next measurement.  Mutually exclusive with ax_ask_divergence_active by construction.

rules.name: ax_impotent_pool_lapse
rules.comment: A21 -- POOL DRIFT, THE ON DIRECTION.  Fires the instant an impotent verdict's OWN pool_agids no longer equals the LIVE _pool_sig() -- i.e. the pool's membership has moved since this verdict minted, whether or not arc_measure_epoch has advanced. Sets pool_stale:1.0.  Deliberately NOT epoch-shaped, the SAME reason A19/A20 gave for their own reversible pairs: a goal can leave the pool (headroom_n -> 0, a status retirement, a further supply/claim resolution) with no epoch bump anywhere in the scene, and 'does this verdict still describe the CURRENT pool' needs the CURRENT truth of that comparison, not a description honest only until the next measurement.  PER-NODE, not a singleton EXISTS guard: every impotent verdict on the graph is independently compared against the SAME live signature, so IM5's multi-verdict history (one verdict per distinct pool composition) is preserved, not collapsed.  Mutually exclusive with ax_impotent_pool_hold by construction (Eq vs Not(Eq) against the same comparison), so the two never contend for the same node in one pass -- the gr_condition_lapse/gr_condition_hold SHAPE and NAMING, reused deliberately: gr_condition_lapse's own ResidualCondition INDIRECTION is not needed here because _pool_sig() is already a live, graph-native Term evaluated inside ax_impotent itself, with no Python probe behind it (unlike fact_equals, which reads a ResidualFact a Python adapter must stamp) -- so a fourth ckind in gr_condition_lapse's closed MISMATCH vocabulary would buy nothing this direct comparison does not already give, at the cost of coupling the GENERIC goal_residuals seed to this seed's own POOL()/_pool_sig() concept.  seeds/goal_residuals.json is BYTE-UNCHANGED by this rule.

rules.name: ax_impotent_pool_hold
rules.comment: A21 -- POOL DRIFT, THE OFF DIRECTION, and not decoration: a one-way lapse would itself be an unrevisable claim -- the gr_condition_lapse/gr_condition_hold precedent, applied directly.  Fires the instant an impotent verdict's pool_agids AGREES with the live _pool_sig() again (true at mint, by construction; also true again if the pool's composition ever returns to exactly what this verdict recorded -- e.g. a re-arm brings a goal back and no further exit has happened) while pool_stale is still 1.0, and restores pool_stale to 0.0. Mutually exclusive with ax_impotent_pool_lapse by construction.

rules.name: ax_ask_impotent
rules.comment: A23 -- CANDIDATE (a), NATIVE FORM (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC6_PREREG.md amendment A23).  `ag_ask` (AG-4) only fires on a VALUE tie; `ax_impotent` fires on the case it cannot see -- a non-empty pool in which NOTHING is routable, no tie required.  Until this rule, an impotent pool went unasked-about entirely: the loop terminated honestly (mints AgendaVerdict{kind:'impotent'}) but said nothing to a human who could name a checkable reason. THE GUARD IS CLASS-SCOPED, NOT GOAL-SCOPED -- this is the whole point of this rule and the reason it is not a copy of ag_ask's own guard.  Keyed to the AgendaVerdict's OWN node identity (Not(Exists(InNeighbours(av, asked_about_verdict), qi, True))), the SAME mint-once-by-signature shape ax_impotent itself already uses for the SAME pool (av mints once per DISTINCT pool_agids, A13/WH4(c)), and the same SHAPE gap_awareness.json's content-dedup guard uses one seed over (note_unresolved_topic_gap/note_reported_gap: file once per distinct content, not once per triggering utterance).  A NAIVE reuse of ag_ask's own re-entry gate -- Not(Exists(ArcQuestion, region==REGION(g), asked_epoch==MEASURE_EPOCH())) -- is keyed PER GOAL, because REGION(g) falls back to g.agid whenever sig_seam is unset, true of every supply_blocker/source_claim/decomposition_tier goal this tree has ever minted (A14 design investigation finding 3), and would therefore re-fire every time testimony drifts nearest_unroutable_agid to a goal not yet asked about BY THAT AGID -- A22 SS3's own measured testimony chain drifts the live winner THREE times inside ONE measurement epoch, on the SAME unchanged 10-goal pool (PROGRAM_SYNTHESIS_ARC6_IMPOTENCE_RESWEEP.md SS3).  Keying to av's own identity instead means the WHOLE CHAIN -- however many times the winner drifts under testimony -- is still describing the SAME impotent state (A14's own headline finding: testimony reweights the pool WITHOUT changing its membership), so it is asked about EXACTLY ONCE.  AR23c measures this live, against a throwaway naive comparator built only in the measurement script (never shipped here). THE QUESTION NAMES THE PRESUPPOSITION EXPLICITLY (design investigation item 3, not a bare testimony request about one goal's content): whether the blocker belongs to the ONE nearest-ranked goal specifically, or to the WHOLE CLASS sharing its kind. DELIBERATELY MINTS NO GoalResidual/testimony -- candidate (b)'s territory (mint-a-capability-goal-adjacent), already NO-GO'd by A22, and out of THIS rule's scope by design: this rule only asks a different question, it does not reprice anything, which is also what keeps AR23c's fixed-point test honest (the ask stopping is never confounded with the pool changing). MINTS A DISTINCT NODE TYPE, ArcImpotenceQuestion, NOT ArcQuestion -- CAUGHT LIVE DURING AR23c's OWN MEASUREMENT, not designed in up front: an ArcQuestion-typed node here would ALSO match ag_reply_mints_testimony_conditioned/unconditioned's own TypeOf(q)=='ArcQuestion' guard (seeds/goal_residuals.json is untouched, but arc_goals.json's two reply rules are generic over EVERY ArcQuestion), so a REPLY to this question would SILENTLY mint testimony too -- exactly candidate (b)'s territory, by accident, defeating the whole 'this rule only asks, it does not reprice' design intent. A distinct type is the SAME cost as the `evidence_artifact`/`source_rid` three-part-key discriminator A15 finding 5 already relies on to keep two ExecClasses from colliding on a shared route: TYPE is the cheapest discriminator this engine has, and it costs zero new rules.

rules.name: ax_ask_impotent_reply
rules.comment: A23 -- closes `ax_ask_impotent`'s own open ArcQuestion when an interlocutor Message responds to it.  Deliberately does NOT mint a GoalResidual/testimony (candidate (a) only, not (b) -- AR23b): this rule only marks the class-scoped question answered, so `ax_ask_impotent`'s own mint-once guard (keyed to the SAME av node) has a stable, observable 'already asked' fact regardless of whether the reply itself ever changes VALUE ranking -- it never will, by this rule's own design.  Matched by TYPE (ArcImpotenceQuestion, not ArcQuestion -- see ax_ask_impotent's own comment for why the type is distinct) AND by the SAME edge its guard reads (asked_about_verdict), so an ordinary ag_ask value-tie question's reply is untouched by this rule, and this rule cannot fire on anything ag_ask minted.
